subject: FintechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP (decision criteria)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>, Jenna Li <jenna.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-07T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: FintechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP (decision criteria)

Hi Samir / Jenna,

Thanks again for your time today 

really appreciated the thoughtful questions. As promised, here's a short recap of the performance and SLO discussion plus a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and decision criteria so we can align next steps. I attached the SLO checklist and a telemetry sample stub.

Quick recap of FintechCo targets we discussed (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for 1k tokens (target for user-facing workflows)
- Tail latency: p99 <= 400ms (critical for UX-sensitive flows)
- Throughput: steady 500 req/s with peaks to 1.5k req/s during batch runs
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent interactive sessions; background batch jobs up to 200 concurrent workers
- Streaming: must support token-by-token streaming to client SDK (low-latency chunked delivery)

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Technical deep-dive w/ Redwood infra team (Aditya + Vivek) — verify p95/p99 with your payloads and streaming behavior (Action: schedule, target this week)
2) Pilot scope: 2-week dedicated trial against a small subset of traffic (~5% production path) with telemetry capture (Action: FintechCo to confirm sample endpoints)
3) Success criteria: p95 <= 225ms, p99 <= 450ms, no functional regressions in output quality, and streaming start latency < 150ms for first token
4) Procurement & legal: finance/procurement to share PO requirements; plan for a 3mo reserved capacity if pilot meets criteria

Decision criteria (what we need to see to recommend production):
- Performance meets success criteria above under expected concurrency and burst patterns
- Observability: access to token-level cost & latency breakdowns + request tracing
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + VPC peering for pilot (if required by your security team)

Next steps (please reply to confirm):
- Confirm the latency/throughput targets or propose adjustments
- Share the telemetry sample endpoints (or we can provide a small load script)
- Availability for a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive with Aditya and Vivek — proposed slots: Thu 9/9 10am PT or Fri 9/10 2pm PT

Attachments: fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx, fintechco-telemetry-sample.jsonl

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jenna Li <jenna.li@fintechco.com>, procure@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-09-07T17:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP (decision criteria)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency targets: the product team asked if we can treat 1k tokens as a normative case but have a separate profile for short-chat (<= 64 tokens) where p95 target should be <= 100ms. Is that feasible?
- Throughput: 500 req/s is accurate for interactive paths, but batch scoring jobs will spike to ~2k req/s for a 10–15 minute window. Can Redwood support these short bursts with reserved capacity or burst credits?
- Streaming: yes, token-by-token streaming is required. Also want to measure time-to-first-byte for streaming start.

We'll send a small telemetry sample tomorrow (JSONL) and confirm which endpoints we want to include in the pilot. Procurement is cc'd; they asked for an outline of the pilot commercial terms (length, what's included, pricing assumptions).

One more thing — for decision criteria, can we include error budget (e.g., <0.5% 5xx during pilot) so both teams have a clear threshold?

Jenna and I are ok with your proposed slots — Thu 9/9 10am PT works.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Engineering, FintechCo
samir.patel@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP (decision criteria)

Thanks for the quick reply, Samir — all good notes. Responses inline: 

- Short-chat profile: yes, we can treat <=64 tokens as a low-latency profile. Proposed target: p95 <= 100ms for short-chat. We'll test both profiles during the pilot.
- Burst capacity: Redwood Dedicated supports burst credits and autoscaling policies. For the pilot we can provision a small reserved pool + burst buffer to cover the 2k spikes; Aditya/Vivek will propose a sizing plan in the deep-dive.
- Streaming start latency: we'll capture time-to-first-byte in the telemetry and include that as a success metric.
- Error budget: happy to include <0.5% 5xx during pilot as part of the acceptance criteria.

Action items I'll take:
- Share a short agenda for Thu 9/9 technical deep-dive (Aditya + Vivek on call)
- Draft pilot commercial outline for procurement (Neha will help with pricing assumptions)

Aditya / Vivek — can you confirm availability for Thu 9/9 10am PT and whether you want any payloads or load shapes in advance?

Samir / Jenna — once you share telemetry endpoints we'll prep the pilot plan and sizing.

Best,
Marissa

All — I'm available Thu 9/9 10am PT. Vivek and I had a quick sync and we'd appreciate the following before the call if possible: 

- A sample request payload and average token counts for the two profiles (short-chat <=64, long-form ~1k)
- Typical concurrency patterns (how many simultaneous interactive users vs. batch workers) and any scheduled batch windows
- Any existing telemetry that shows p95/p99 currently observed (if you can share a few representative traces)

If you can't share payloads ahead of time, we can run a couple of synthetic load shapes during the call. I’ll prepare an initial sizing sketch for a pilot reserved pool that covers 500 steady req/s with a 2x burst buffer (so up to 1k steady and short 2k spikes) and we’ll refine after we see actual telemetry.

See you Thu.
